newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end higher, ignore Dow weakness.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end higher, ignore Dow weakness.

text.p: French shares shrugged off Wall Street's weakness to settle slightly higher on Thursday after fluctuating between negative and positive territory throughout the day.
Shares pushed higher late in the afternoon and traders said the advance was likely related to the end of the October account. "There were probably some exercises on the option side," one trader said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index traded in a narrow 13-point range during the day. It finished up 0.13 percent or 2.76 points at 2,151.62. The CAC-40 futures contract settled three points higher at 2,157.0. Volume totalled 5.18 billion francs.

"Trade at the moment is very technical, with shares trading very close to their support and resistance levels," one trader said. "It is a fairly healthy pause," he said, adding his target for the CAC-40 for year-end was 2,250.

Traders said the market should be supported on Friday by buying at the start of the new account. "The market is consolidating an exceptionally good month in volumes we haven't experienced for a very long time," said one trader.
Traders said the bourse was underpinned by a relatively good first-half earnings season and were upbeat about its prospects even with the economy showing no signs of emerging from its doldrums.

"We have some really strong earners in the CAC which are not French companies per se like L'Oreal that have a lot of external earnings," said one. "A lot have a heavy dependence on the United States, which is doing quite well."
Computer-aided design and engineering software maker Dassault Systemes ended up 3.24 percent at 216.50 francs after reporting nine-month profits jumped to 209.7 million francs from 117.4 million.
French chemical and drugs group Rhone-Poulenc, due to report its third quarter earnings on Friday, rose 0.85 percent at 142.50 francs.
